rulings.ruling: Ruling: equivalent; project retained. With no gambling winnings line 8b is zero, so the smaller of the losses and line 8b is zero, which the project writes as an explicit zero; with winnings both give the losses up to line 8b (i1040sca p. 11, Other Itemized Deductions, "Gambling losses ... but only to the extent of gambling winnings reported on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8b"; decision D14). The project's guard asks the losses only of a filer with winnings.

Ruling: equivalent representation; project retained. The second transcription applies the State and Local Tax Deduction Worksheet only when modified AGI exceeds $500,000 or income was excluded, and otherwise takes the $40,000 base directly; the project computes the worksheet unconditionally, where the reduction is zero at or below the threshold and the excluded-income case is refused (`sa.excluded_income`). Same value within scope (i1040sca p. 7).

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. Both test whether your own person entry answers yes to born before January 2, 1961: the project as a count above zero, the second as a count of at least one; a count is a whole number, so the tests agree (i1040gi p. 33, Line 12d, "If you or your spouse (if you are married and filing a joint return) were born before January 2, 1961").

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; project retained. Both select the itemized total (line 17) when itemizing is elected, when a separate-return spouse itemizes, or when line 17 exceeds the standard deduction, and the standard deduction otherwise, with the standard deduction zero when a separate-return spouse itemizes and increased by the age and blindness additions. As on `sa.itemizes`, the project conditions the spouse-itemizes rule on married-filing-separately status, which the second transcription omits; married filing separately is refused (`s3.married`, spec 2.2), so within scope the selections agree (i1040gi pp. 34–35, line 12e and the Standard Deduction Chart).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; project retained. After the fix of BUG-0084 both transcriptions count the age box only for a person who did not die in 2025 before reaching 65 (i1040gi p. 33, Line 12d, Death of spouse in 2025; p501 p. 23). The one difference left is the spouse-itemizes condition for married filing separately (the project's standard deduction is zero when the spouse itemizes on a separate return), which the second omits; married filing separately is refused (s3.mfs), as ruled before.
